title: Level design
author: Embarrassed-Plan8108
selftext: Has anyone had any luck with realistic level design? I decided to see if AI could help as to I'm struggling with making and FPS map and I'm not sure if my prompts are terrible but they are worse than what I made

comments.author: muikrad
comments.body: I think that's the kind of thing you need a human for. AI will just do it randomly and inconsistently.

comments.author: PM_Me_Those_
comments.body: You might be able to do it with AI but you probably need to have a very very good description of what you want or a reasonably accurate sketch of what you're looking for. I would not give AI the 'reigns' on creating good level design on its own, it's already quite mediocre at other similar aspects of game design.

comments.author: TheEverdepth
comments.body:
I think level design is something that really needs an experienced human touch to make it really polished. You're not going to be able to fart out something that is memorable, plays and looks great, and immerses the player within a cohesive world. 

But if you're struggling with that, I'd suggest 2 options:

1. Work on defining a ruleset for level generation that reflects what you're going for and have it work within those parameters. Kind of just prompt refining, but that's helped me for early prototyping. the levels will still feel fairly randomly generated in parts, and depends on the game how much this matters 
2. Have AI build you a basic in-game level designer that allows you to work from its base and tweak the specific things you want and get that extra custom touch. This also helps you learn what matters to you about getting the right layout or design, which might be the most important part

Combining these together has worked ok for me, but I'm still learning myself so take that for what it's worth.

replies.author: Embarrassed-Plan8108
replies.body: I appreciate it. It seems like level design has been the hardest part of this

comments.author: 2nd_breakfastt
comments.body:
Tell your ai agent to research popular fps games and their map layouts. 

Have it research and answer a few questions: what makes a good fps map? What makes an fps map fun? What makes a good design in fps maps? Etc. 

When making your project, have your agent keep these running docs: game bible, art bible, ideas, problems. Your agent should keep these updated as you progress through development. This will help your agent keep track of what it’s done, what to do, and future ideas

Once your agent has done the research, tell it to help you to design an fps map, using anything that it researched to apply to your project. Tell it to help brainstorm with you first, and then together you can design your map

After the research is done and you read through it, I’d prompt it with something like: Using the research that you just did, help me brainstorm ideas regarding map design for an fps game for my project. Do you understand? Do you have any questions before you start? Anything you’d like to add?

I like to end some prompts with those two questions, to make sure the agent understands its task, and if it has any questions or anything to add before it begins its process. Let me know how that helps!

replies.author: Embarrassed-Plan8108
replies.body: I very much appreciate this! Thank you

replies.author: 2nd_breakfastt
replies.body:
To go further on this, if you’re also looking for help with your art style and overall look of the game, the same process can apply

Once your agent develops your art bible, upload the art bible to another ai agent to review and analyze it to see if they would change, remove, add anything (you should also do this with your game bible). Then once the art bible is made, ask your agent to give you prompts to generate reference images for your game (eventually your assets, ui, etc). Generate those images and tweak them until you like what you see

Then along with your prompt, upload the reference images, and have it try to replicate the images the best it can. (Lot more steps to the process but this is a quick rundown)

replies.author: caesium23
replies.body: Yep! I had an agent research map design and it came up with a bunch of principles like needing loops, cover, etc. It's maps are still pretty trash, but at least they all meet those minimum gameplay requirements now. Getting better just requires adding more instructions.

comments.author: fisj
comments.body: Level design isn't something AI does well at this point. AI is barely getting it's handle on spatial reasoning for assets. It may be a long while before AI can do LD well, since LD is also highly genre dependent.

comments.author: CharlesFXD
comments.body: My first thought was find a nice street map for an area you like. One with drawn streets and building outlines. Then find the satellite view Google maps. Maybe even the 3D view from google from 4 directions. N, S, E, W and see what your AI can do with it. Assuming it’s a place that takes place on Earth. Then touch it up. Make dead ends when necessary etc in a 3d level designer you ask it to build for you.

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: Yes I’ve gotten Codex to do petty decent level design by having it study my mechanics and then using a data driven method that considers movement, line of sight, distance between key points, cover etc. Then it runs bot simulations for balance and to determine how much of an advantage is attained by being more skilled. Then I play against bots and friends and iterate.

replies.author: Embarrassed-Plan8108
replies.body: Is that another version of Claude

replies.author: SeasawPhilosopher
replies.body: Codex is OpenAIs coding agent, so yes similar. Although at this point I’ve switched to Claude Code as I find it better, but back when I was doing level design I was still using Codex.

replies.author: Embarrassed-Plan8108
replies.body: Level design is the only thing I'm struggling with

comments.author: Hotwingz66
comments.body:
Maybe this helps, there a lot of gdc talks on youtube.

This might not be a shortcut like prompting but I think you are going to want some advice from experts to evaluate the feeling of a map when you build one.

If you dont have a natural feel for flow, it also just helps by thinking in blocks. What is my level supposed to do. How can I do it. How do I guide the player towards my objective. What are fun problem/solutions along the way.
